newsitem.title: UK: Carlton buys Rank film distribution arm.
newsitem.headline: Carlton buys Rank film distribution arm.

text.p: Rank Group Plc said Wednesday that it sold its film distribution unit to Carlton Communications Plc for 65 million pounds ($107 million), sealing its transition from a "golden era" movie-maker to a modern film services and leisure firm.

The sale completed Rank's disposal of 300 million pounds ($493 million) worth of non-core assets about 10 months ahead of schedule and added classic films directed by David Lean and Alfred Hitchcock to Carlton's movie library.

"Following today's sale of Rank Film Distributors Ltd, our film and entertainment services division is now clearly focused on serving the film industry, primarily the major Hollywood studios," Chief Executive Andrew Teare said.

The deal gives Carlton a catalogue of 740 features to help feed its appetite for film and TV content, particularly after its digital broadcasting pact with Granada Group Plc and British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc.
Carlton Chairman Michael Green said the Rank Film library should help to ensure advertiser support for Carlton's planned film channel on digital terrestrial television.

The Rank library, which dates back to the 1930s, included titles from the British film industry's heyday, including Hitchcock's "The Lady Vanishes" and Lean's "Great Expectations," as well as recent productions like "Fried Green Tomatoes" and "The Shawshank Redemption."
Rank, once a strong presence in British film-making, has concentrated increasingly on leisure activities such as its Hard Rock Cafe brand in the last couple of decades.
In the past eight months, Rank has sold about 11 non-core businesses as part of its disposal programme.
Rank said it would use proceeds from the sale of Rank Film Distribution to reduce debt.
